stories.headline: US launches Operation Economic Outcast to isolate Iran with sweeping sanctions
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a major sanctions campaign against Iran on August 24, 2026 [c1]. President Donald Trump directed the launch of Operation Economic Outcast [c1]. The operation targets Iran and its foreign enablers [c1]. Bessent said the objective is to cut off every economic lifeline that sustains the Iranian regime [c2]. He said Tehran must be left standing completely alone [c2].

Bessent announced an unprecedented global economic war against all Iranian revenue streams [c20]. The effort directly targets Iran's oil revenue [c20]. He named five key sectors supporting the Iranian economy [c8]. These sectors are digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping [c8]. They will all face heightened scrutiny from the United States [c8]. Bessent warned that any entity helping Iran wash money will face strict penalties [c11]. They will be removed from the US dollar financial system [c11].

Bessent said Trump is personally calling world leaders [c9]. Trump is asking them to stop all economic dealings with Tehran [c9]. Bessent pointed to recent actions by the United Arab Emirates as proof of diplomatic success [c10]. The country suspended trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran [c10].

Iran warned it would stop all regional oil exports if the conflict with the US continues [c15]. The regime also warned ships not to cross the Strait of Hormuz without permission [c16]. Economist David Oxley said about 90% of Iran's oil exports go to China [c17]. Oxley works as chief climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics [c17]. On August 24, 2026, Brent crude oil reached $92 per barrel [c18]. Gasoline prices in the United States went over $4 per gallon [c19].

The US dollar index rose 0.17 percent to 98.99 on August 24, 2026 [c12]. This increase came after the US announced expanded sanctions [c12]. CNBC reported that Bessent could use the Treasury General Account [c13]. The account holds near $1 trillion at the Federal Reserve [c13]. He could use it to fund bond buybacks [c13].

The market actions also affected Canada [c14]. The Canadian dollar fell 0.61 percent to C$1.385 per US dollar on August 24, 2026 [c14]. Trump threatened to raise tariffs on Canadian goods to 50% on January 1, 2027 [c6]. These goods include cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel [c6]. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said this threat was expected [c7]. Carney asked what message it sends to US workers who rely on Canadian demand [c7]. He mentioned workers in states like Michigan and Ohio [c7].

Public support for the war has dropped among Americans [c3]. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed support fell to 31% [c3]. This was down from 34% earlier in August 2026 [c3]. Among Republicans, 69% support the war with Iran [c4]. That is down from 77% in March [c4]. Recent polling showed Trump's approval rating at a low of 33% [c5].

stories.headline: US-Canada trade negotiations collapse as Trump threatens 50 percent auto tariffs
stories.body:
Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed after both sides failed to reach an agreement [c21]. Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel [c22]. The new tax starts on January 1, 2027 [c22].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations and recalled his team to Ottawa [c32]. Carney said Canada rejected the US terms because of last-minute demands [c31]. He said those demands limited tariff relief and restricted Canada's trade independence [c31]. Carney said Canada will return to talks only when the US acts like a true partner [c23]. An Angus Reid Institute poll showed three in four Canadians supported his decision to walk away [c28].

Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Trump declared economic war on Canada [c25]. Ford warned Canada could cut off electricity and critical minerals to the US [c26]. Industry leader Flavio Volpe warned that tariffs on auto parts would stop US car assembly [c27].

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the US had to act after Canadian retaliation [c30]. Annual trade between the two nations reached about $909 billion [c24]. On August 24, shares of Ford fell 3.2%, Stellantis fell 4.7%, and General Motors fell 1.1% [c29]. Trump claimed on Truth Social that Canadian farm tariffs created a $60 billion trade deficit [c33].

stories.headline: Britain expands Ukraine military support with missile technology and AI partnership
stories.body:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Kyiv on August 24, 2026 [c38]. This was his first official trip abroad as prime minister [c38]. Burnham and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a new defense AI partnership [c42]. Britain became the first foreign partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs [c42].

The deal allows the UK to use AI models trained on Ukrainian battlefield data [c34]. This technology will protect British military sites and infrastructure [c34]. The Avengers database contains 5 million battlefield images from the DELTA combat management system [c43]. These AI systems analyze over 100,000 drone video feeds monthly and spot about 70 percent of targets in real time [c44]. Burnham said this work will speed up security efforts [c36]. The UK Ministry of Defence approved AI projects with British tech companies Sintela, Mind Foundry, and Skyral [c35].

The UK also allowed defense firm MBDA to share declassified details on Scalp cruise missiles [c39]. This enables Ukraine to make missile components locally [c39]. The missile measures 5.10 metres long and weighs about 1,300 kg [c45]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the transfer undermines peace efforts [c40]. He said Russian forces are searching for production sites [c40].

Britain has given over £25 billion in military and civilian help to Ukraine since 2022 [c46]. Meanwhile, the European Union released €6.1 billion in military aid [c41]. Former intelligence officer Dr. Frank Ledwidge said European commitments fail to solve Kyiv's need for air defence interceptors [c37].

stories.headline: US Department of Homeland Security proposes 103,265 dollar H-1B visa fee
stories.body:
The US Department of Homeland Security published a new rule in the Federal Register on Monday [c58]. The rule proposes a new $103,265 fee for cap-subject H-1B visa petitions [c47]. This proposal opens a 30-day public comment period [c58]. Officials could finalize the new rule by the end of 2026 [c64].

The H-1B program allows American employers to hire foreign workers for specialty jobs [c63]. The visa lasts up to three years initially [c63]. It can be extended up to six years total [c63]. The government sets an annual cap of 85,000 new visas [c51]. This total includes 65,000 regular visas and 20,000 visas reserved under the Master's cap [c51]. US Citizenship and Immigration Services already received enough petitions to reach both caps for fiscal year 2027 [c67].

The proposed $103,265 charge is an extra payment [c49]. It comes on top of existing filing fees and statutory costs [c49]. Before recent increases, government fees for H-1B visas usually ranged from $2,000 to $5,000 [c60]. In August, officials introduced extra fees of up to $4,500 for extension or transfer requests [c62].

An earlier $100,000 fee was introduced in September 2025 through a presidential proclamation [c48]. That fee expires in September 2026 unless extended [c48]. However, legal battles have blocked that requirement [c65]. On June 8, 2026, a federal judge in Massachusetts struck down guidance implementing the $100,000 fee [c65]. On July 24, 2026, an appeals court refused to pause that ruling [c66]. As of February 15, only 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee for 85 workers [c59].

Legal expert Mitch Wexler said the proposed $103,265 fee depends on whether a petition is cap-subject, not worker location [c52]. Higher education institutions and affiliated non-profit groups will not pay the fee [c50]. Research organizations are also exempt [c50]. New York immigration lawyer Cyrus D Mehta called the fee preposterous [c53]. He said the government killed the goose that laid the golden eggs [c53].

Government officials estimate the fee will raise $8.78 billion each year [c56]. They estimate 14,541 small businesses will be affected [c57]. For 76% of those businesses, costs will rise by more than 1% of annual revenue [c57].

Indian workers rely heavily on the program [c54]. In fiscal year 2025, Indian citizens received 283,000 H-1B visas including extensions [c54]. That was 70% of all visas given [c54]. Indian workers also got nearly 58,000 new visas for initial employment [c55].

Overall interest in the program has dropped [c61]. Employers registered for about 344,000 visas last year [c61]. That was down over 25 percent from 2024 [c61]. It was far below the 794,000 registrations in 2023 [c61]. Boundless Immigration CEO Xiao Wang said top sponsors now include Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Google [c68]. Company data showed senior Level III candidates had a 68% selection rate in March 2026 [c69]. Entry-level Level I candidates had a 40% rate [c69].

Lawmakers have also introduced the End H-1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026 [c70]. It proposes a three-year pause on new visas, a cap of 25,000, and a $200,000 minimum salary threshold [c70].
